category_title: Students with mild intellectual disability capable of logical leadership roles
minimal_context: Ben is sitting at a computer in the classroom to review his homework on Google Drive and set new learning goals.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Ben, it is time for self-evaluation. Please open your homework on Google Drive so we can set new goals and find out what you have to improve.

STUDENT: I don't want to look at the Drive. I don't want to do this right now.

TUTOR: What do you think you should pay more attention to for the next steps of your learning tasks?

STUDENT: Study. Good.

TUTOR: Can you write down a full sentence about your suggestions for your new goals?

STUDENT: (Sighs, looking frustrated) No. Just... read. Better.

options.A: Extend lessons to one and a half hours, unlike in mainstream schools where normal lessons last between 40 and 50 minutes.
options.B: Use desk carrels during self-evaluation to provide areas of personal space and make a clear distinction between individual and group activity areas.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the self-evaluation and goal-setting tasks on Google Drive during the session.
options.D: Provide noncontingent attention throughout the evaluation session and ignore the problem behaviors that function to gain attention.
